match.reason: No point in the bank teaches external stability itself: the balance of payments point covers what is in the current account and the objectives point lists a sustainable balance of payments, but neither covers sustainable foreign liabilities or currency stability.

draft.title: What external stability means
card: External stability is about a country's dealings with the rest of the world. An economy is externally stable when it can keep those dealings going without a crisis.
the current account deficit and the foreign liabilities (foreign debt and foreign equity) can be financed and serviced over time without forcing sharp cuts in spending.
the exchange rate is not prone to sharp swings. It can move, but large sudden falls or rises make trade and borrowing harder to plan.
Stability does not mean a balanced current account. A deficit can be sustained if foreign investors keep lending and the income owed abroad stays manageable.
draft.remember: External stability means a sustainable deficit and liabilities, and a currency without sharp swings.

a.q: Which description best fits an externally stable economy?
opts: Its deficit and debts can be sustained and its dollar is steady
Its current account is always in exact balance with others
Its exchange rate is fixed and never changes from year to year
Its foreign liabilities are zero, so it owes nothing abroad
a.why: Stability is about whether the deficit and liabilities can be sustained and whether the currency avoids sharp swings. It does not need a balanced account, because a deficit can be sustained. That is why the balanced account option is wrong.
a.clue: Stability is about sustainability, not zero deficit.

b.q: Country X has run a current account deficit for years. Foreign investors keep lending to it, and its dollar moves only gently. How is its external stability best described?
opts: Stable, as the deficit is sustained and the dollar is steady
Unstable, as any current account deficit signals weakness
Unstable, because the dollar moves at all from week to week
Stable, but only because its deficit is falling to zero
b.why: Lenders keep financing the deficit and the currency is not swinging sharply, so the economy is externally stable. The tempting answer says any deficit means instability, but the card says a deficit can be sustained.
b.clue: Ask whether the deficit can be kept going, not whether it exists.

proposal.title: What external stability means
card: External stability is about a country's dealings with the rest of the world. An economy is externally stable when it can keep those dealings going without a crisis.
the current account deficit and the foreign liabilities (foreign debt and foreign equity) can be financed and serviced over time without forcing sharp cuts in spending.
the exchange rate is not prone to sharp swings. It can move, but large sudden falls or rises make trade and borrowing harder to plan.
Stability does not mean a balanced current account. A deficit can be sustained if foreign investors keep lending and the income owed abroad stays manageable.
proposal.remember: Two tests: a deficit and liabilities that can be carried, and a currency without sharp swings.

a.q: An economy runs a current account deficit. Which fact best suggests it is still externally stable?
opts: Foreign investors keep lending to it year after year
Its exchange rate has fallen sharply in recent months
Its income owed abroad is rising faster than it can pay
It needed sharp spending cuts to meet its debt payments
a.why: A deficit can be sustained while foreign investors keep lending and the income owed abroad stays manageable. A sharp fall in the exchange rate is the most tempting option, but sharp swings in the currency are a sign of instability, not stability.
a.clue: Which fact shows the deficit can keep being financed?

b.q: Country X has a current account deficit that foreign lenders fund easily, and its currency moves gently. Country Y has a surplus, but its currency often jumps or plunges within a month. Which is externally stable?
opts: X, as lenders fund its deficit and its currency is calm
Y, as a surplus shows it is the stronger external position
Both, as each one can pay its way with the rest of the world
Neither, as a deficit and sharp swings both signal trouble
b.why: X passes both tests: its deficit is financed and its currency is not prone to sharp swings. Y is tempting because it has a surplus, but stability does not depend on the current account balance alone, and Y's currency swings sharply.
b.clue: Check each country against both tests, not just the current account.
